Can we understand a bit better who’s being blamed here? The original article blamed “systematic funds” or trend-following strategies, which is honestly some of the oldest and tiresome excuses for market volatility that I just don’t believe to be true. 

And then all the replies and quotes seem to have moved onto the “incentive structures at these funds”. A systematic trend-following strategy has no incentives structure. It’s fully systematic and non-discretionary at inception. 

What they seem to be alluding at is the incentive structure at the multistrat discretionary equity pods with tight risk budgets that offer almost a real call option. Do pods have an incentive to crowd into the same momentum trades. Well I guess I can see that esp during a bubble. But someone should document it. 

What I don’t know is if pods are any likelier to be crowded into the same momentum trades and rush for the exit causing large market drawdowns. See the behaviors of HFs documented during the DotCom Bubble, before multistrats were even popular. It was the same exact thing. 

In fact, if anything we should celebrate and marvel at the fact that despite the proliferation of systematic strategies and crowded trades at the pods what not, volatility at the aggregate market level remains historically low despite the extraordinary bull run. VIX or volatility on SPX, where most of the money sits is well below the levels reached in the late 90s and 2000s even with the gyrations and degen meme trades extra. 

If this isn’t market efficiency I don’t know what is.

I know this is a predictable opinion from me but I don't agree with the strong emotional reaction against the anti-data-center movements that I've seen this week.

As I see it, algorithmic progress means that whatever you would be able to do with more and bigger data centers in 2 years, you will be able to do with the data centers we have today in 4 years - probably sooner. So nothing remotely apocalyptically bad will happen from even extreme levels of success by anti-data-center people.

Meanwhile we need all the time we can get to better harden the world against both already-visible cybersecurity issues and any bio and other risks soon to come. Science applications are bottlenecked by many things other than AI, so slowing AI down by one year will slow those down by much less than one year.

Given this, a slowdown in compute hyper-scaling seems quite net good? Notice this is without any controversial "doomer arguments", RSI etc. Even if net-bad, it's certainly not worse than like 10+ other political things.

Chamath: “I got it totally wrong. This election was a complete and total repudiation about the state of the economy. The economy is broken.”

“What I don't think I understood clearly enough, and I think that this election has made it extremely clear, is that since COVID, we have moved past political ideology.

And I want to say this again, I do not think Democrats or Republicans matter. That is my real takeaway after this election.

There is a central bloc of people that vote on the prescient issues of our time. What are these people voting for? I think what they are shouting now, they were trying to signal, and now they are shouting, is a broad-based belief that the economy has completely decoupled from reality and is broken.

The economic reality in America is broken.

There is a small percentage of people, the four of us on this pod and all of our friends, who are the asset owners of America, and we have benefited in every weather condition.

When rates were zero, we benefited because we were able to build our businesses with very cheap capital. When rates were high, we benefited because we had pricing power. And in every condition in between, we've all managed to continue to accumulate and grow assets, but we are few and far between.

And then there's everybody else who are wage earners, and the structural capacity of the American economy to support and grow wage earners is broken.

I don't think this has anything to do with socialism. I don't think the far left won particularly more than they were expected to. I don't think the far right won particularly more than was expected.

This was a complete and total repudiation about the state of the economy. The economy is broken.”

David Sacks: Trump Can Save His Second Term by Ending the Iran War

Sacks:

“Your question was, ‘Can Trump fix this?’ I think absolutely.”

Jason:

“What's your top three things he can do to fix it?”

Sacks:

“Just get out of the war. That's my number one, my number two, and my number three.

Because what will happen, the price of Brent crude will drop precipitously.

On the day of the election, the price of Brent crude dropped 10%.

Is that because something changed in the Strait of Hormuz? No. It's because the market started to price in the mere possibility that the war would end sooner, and we got a 10% cut in the price of Brent crude.

It will go from $110 to $70 (per barrel) if this war ends. Gas prices will drop. Diesel will drop. The price of food will drop.

And then the underlying strong economic growth, the GDP growth, and the employment picture, which are still robust, will come into focus. And I think that Trump's popularity will rebound and be back in the 40s.

That's the thing we need to do. And if we don't do that, if the war continues, the Republicans will continue to bleed popularity.”

tweets.text:
I like @omarchy! I can be wrong, but I don't see it replacing people's operating system since OS are so tightly coupled with the hardware. I do think it's the next operating system for agents, and soon more agents will use operating system than humans anyway! 

There is something so beautiful about using a coding agent to create every app, every plugin, everything in your computer. You can look at my theme it's retro-futuristic French Napoleonic Empire; it was just a prompt. I also have all sorts of super custom apps to fit my workflows. The future is ultra-personalized software. 

We've spent decades designing operating systems around human interaction. We're entering an era where software agents will be first-class users of those systems, and the most programmable environments will have a huge advantage! You should try it, it's a very cool project by @dhh and team.
